title: Rank-one projectable embedding identifiability theorem
question: Do the rank-one kinetic condition and the existence of at most one finite pole uniquely determine the algebraic/potential matrix and action-derived source direction needed for a full projectable ADM embedding?

frozen_setup.kinetic_matrix: K=kappa*v*v^T with v=(1,a)^T and kappa nonzero
frozen_setup.source_vector: s=(s1,s2)^T independent of v unless an action principle fixes it

required_exact_checks: finite pole location depends on M and v but not on source vector s
response numerator/residue depends on source vector s
two non-collinear source vectors can share the same pole denominator but have different static responses
there exists a continuous family of symmetric invertible M with the same chosen finite pole for fixed rank-one K
therefore rank-one plus one-pole data do not uniquely source-lock the full embedding

decision_rule.IDENTIFIABLE: Only if both M and s are uniquely determined by the frozen information.
decision_rule.NON_IDENTIFIABLE_PASS_SCOPED: If exact algebra exhibits at least one continuous ambiguity in M or s while preserving the same rank-one/one-pole structure.

scope: Structural identifiability only. A NON_IDENTIFIABLE result is not a no-go for rank-one completion; it means an additional independently motivated action principle is required before rerunning s6fT.
